context.analysis:
## Overview
- An Amazon-style multi-currency e-commerce platform hosted on AWS for physical and electronic book sales.
- Designed to handle 1 million monthly active users globally while ensuring strict GDPR/CCPA and OWASP compliance.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer & Reviewer (Person)
- Store Administrator (Person)
- Online Bookstore System (Software System)
- External Payment Gateway (External System)
- Third-Party Shipping Provider API (External System)
- External Recommendation Service (External System)

## Relationships
- Book Buyer/Reviewer to Online Bookstore System via HTTPS / TLS 1.3
- Store Administrator to Online Bookstore System via HTTPS / TLS 1.3 (with MFA)
- Online Bookstore System to External Payment Gateway via REST over TLS 1.3 / mTLS
- Online Bookstore System to Third-Party Shipping API via REST/Webhook over TLS 1.3 / mTLS with HMAC
- Online Bookstore System to External Recommendation Service via gRPC/REST over TLS 1.3

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Platform: AWS (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`) for multi-region scalability and high availability.
- Orchestration: Amazon EKS / Serverless for containerized workloads meeting performance SLAs.
- Security & Compliance: AWS KMS for data-at-rest encryption and AWS Secrets Manager for dynamic credential rotation.
- Integration Protocols: TLS 1.3, mTLS, and HMAC for secure, encrypted, and authenticated external communication.

## Rationale
- Multi-region AWS deployment guarantees 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads globally for 1M MAU.
- Strict TLS 1.3, mTLS, and AWS encryption mechanisms satisfy GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP Top-10 security requirements.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style e-commerce site for physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews, designed for global scale, strict compliance, and high availability.]

## Key Elements
- Users: Book Buyer & Reviewer, Store Administrator, Marketing/Merchandising Specialist
- External Systems: External Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping Provider API, External Recommendation Service
- Containers: Single-Page Application (SPA), Admin / Back-Office App, Amazon API Gateway, Core E-Commerce API (Node.js/NestJS), Recommendation Service (Python/FastAPI), Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Infrastructure: AWS S3, CloudFront, ECS Fargate, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS

## Relationships
- SPA & Admin App -> HTTPS -> Amazon API Gateway (REST/GraphQL)
- API Gateway -> mTLS -> Core E-Commerce API & Recommendation Service
- Core E-Commerce API -> TLS over TCP -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & ElastiCache
- Core E-Commerce API -> gRPC -> Recommendation Service
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon SQS -> Third-Party Shipping Provider API
- Admin App -> Amazon EventBridge -> Core API & Recommendation Service

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React / TypeScript on AWS S3 & CloudFront for <2s page load performance
- Core Backend: Node.js (NestJS) on AWS ECS (Fargate) for scalable e-commerce logic
- Recommendation Engine: Python (FastAPI) on AWS ECS (Fargate)
- Database & Caching: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ) and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Messaging & Integration: Amazon EventBridge and Amazon SQS
- Security: AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, OAuth2/OIDC, JWT, mTLS

## Rationale
- Decouples revenue-generating storefront operations from administrative and analytical workloads to protect checkout availability and performance.
- Utilizes asynchronous event-driven patterns via SQS and EventBridge to ensure resilience against third-party shipping API degradation.

Single-Page Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
The Single-Page Application (SPA) serves as the primary frontend interface for the Online Bookstore, enabling users to browse, purchase, and review books. It is built to deliver high-performance, secure e-commerce experiences while supporting 1 million monthly active users globally.

## Key Elements
* Router & State Management Module (Redux Toolkit / Zustand)
* Catalog & Search View
* Checkout & Cart Workflow (supporting guest and authenticated flows)
* Review & Rating Component (DOMPurify for sanitization)
* API Client (Axios / GraphQL client with interceptors)

## Relationships
* Book Buyer & Reviewer -> Single-Page Application (SPA): Browses catalog, manages cart, and submits reviews [HTTPS]
* Single-Page Application (SPA) -> Amazon API Gateway: Communicates API requests and authentication flows [HTTPS (REST/GraphQL)]

## Technology Stack
* React / TypeScript: Chosen for component reusability and fast UI rendering.
* AWS S3 & CloudFront: Selected for static asset hosting and low-latency global edge caching.
* DOMPurify: Utilized for client-side input sanitization against XSS.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures sub-2-second page loads on 3G networks and meets strict OWASP Top-10 security standards. Decoupling the frontend presentation layer from backend pricing and calculations safeguards multi-currency transactions and prevents client-side tampering.

Admin / Back-Office App.analysis:
## Overview
The Admin / Back-Office App is a secure web application enabling store administrators, marketing specialists, and support staff to manage catalog inventory, merchandising campaigns, GDPR/CCPA compliance requests, and order exceptions. It ensures operational oversight and regulatory adherence while maintaining a strict security boundary from the public e-commerce store.

## Key Elements
- Store Administrator: Manages store operations and catalog
- Marketing/Merchandising Specialist: Manages marketing campaigns and promotions
- Support Staff: Resolves shipping integrations and payment discrepancies
- Admin / Back-Office App Container: Angular/TypeScript SPA hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront
- Catalog Management Component: Handles inventory CRUD operations
- Merchandising & Campaign Component: Manages promotions and recommendation overrides
- User Data & Compliance Component: Executes secure GDPR/CCPA data export and deletion workflows
- Audit Logging Service: Captures administrative state changes
- Order & Exception Operations Component: Powers the Reconciliation Dashboard
- Analytics & Reporting Component: Renders promotion performance metrics
- Amazon API Gateway: Secure entry point using REST/GraphQL over HTTPS
- Amazon EventBridge: Receives immutable audit logs via AWS SDK

## Relationships
- Store Administrator -> Admin / Back-Office App: Manages store operations [HTTPS]
- Marketing/Merchandising Specialist -> Admin / Back-Office App: Manages campaigns [HTTPS]
- Support Staff -> Admin / Back-Office App: Resolves order exceptions [HTTPS]
- Admin / Back-Office App -> Amazon API Gateway: Makes administrative API requests [HTTPS (REST/GraphQL)]
- Audit Logging Service -> Amazon EventBridge: Publishes audit events [AWS SDK / API]

## Technology Stack
- Frontend SPA: Angular with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS for responsive UI design
- Hosting Infrastructure: AWS S3 & CloudFront for performant static asset delivery and global reach
- API Layer: Amazon API Gateway (REST/GraphQL over HTTPS) for secure request routing and RBAC enforcement
- Integration & Logging: AWS SDK and Amazon EventBridge for immutable audit log transmission and asynchronous eventing

## Rationale
This architecture isolates sensitive administrative workflows behind multi-factor authentication and strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), satisfying GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP security mitigations. Utilizing Angular on AWS S3/CloudFront paired with API Gateway ensures high availability (99.95% uptime) and low-latency back-office operations.

Amazon API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a scalable global e-commerce online bookstore serving 1M MAU with multi-currency support, secure checkout, and personalized recommendations. The architecture leverages AWS managed services and microservices to ensure high availability, low latency, and strict GDPR/CCPA compliance.]

## Key Elements
*   **Users:** Book Buyer & Reviewer, Store Administrator
*   **Clients:** Single-Page Application (SPA) (React / TypeScript on AWS S3 & CloudFront), Admin / Back-Office App
*   **Gateway Layer:** Amazon API Gateway
*   **API Gateway Components:** WAF Integration Component, Edge Router & SSL Terminating Proxy, Authorizer Component, Throttling & Rate Limiter, API Router & Transformer, Analytics & Metrics Component
*   **Backend Services:** Core E-Commerce API (Node.js/NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate), Recommendation Service (Python/FastAPI on AWS ECS Fargate)
*   **Data & Messaging:** Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ), Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS
*   **External Systems:** External Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping Provider API, External Recommendation Service

## Relationships
*   Single-Page Application -> Amazon API Gateway: Makes API requests via HTTPS (REST/GraphQL)
*   Admin App -> Amazon API Gateway: Makes administrative API requests via HTTPS (REST/GraphQL)
*   AWS WAF -> Edge Router: Inspects and forwards clean traffic via HTTPS
*   API Router & Transformer -> Core E-Commerce API: Routes validated requests via mTLS over VPC Links
*   API Router & Transformer -> Recommendation Service: Routes recommendation requests via mTLS over VPC Links

## Technology Stack
*   **API Gateway:** AWS API Gateway with Lambda Authorizers, Usage Plans, and VPC Links for secure routing and scalability.
*   **Security:** AWS WAF for edge protection against OWASP Top-10 threats; TLS 1.3 and mTLS for data-in-transit.
*   **Compute:** AWS ECS (Fargate) running Node.js (NestJS) and Python (FastAPI) for containerized microservices.
*   **Database & Cache:** Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ) for transactional data; Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for performance caching.
*   **Messaging:** Amazon EventBridge and Amazon SQS for asynchronous event-driven communication.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses AWS managed services and a containerized microservices pattern to easily scale past 1M MAU while guaranteeing 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads. Offloading edge security, rate limiting, and JWT validation to Amazon API Gateway and AWS WAF directly protects backend ECS workloads and satisfies strict GDPR/CCPA compliance.]

Core E-Commerce API.analysis:
## Overview
The Core E-Commerce API is a NestJS container on AWS ECS Fargate that orchestrates business logic for the Online Bookstore. It securely handles catalog browsing, shopping carts, secure checkouts, and multi-currency transactions.

## Key Elements
- Catalog Controller & Service (NestJS)
- Cart & Checkout Engine (NestJS)
- Currency Conversion Provider (NestJS)
- Feature Flag Module (AWS AppConfig / Unleash SDK)
- Idempotency Interceptor (NestJS / Redis)
- Payment & Shipping Gateway Adapters (NestJS / Circuit Breaker)
- Order Event Publisher (NestJS / Amazon EventBridge / Amazon SQS)

## Relationships
- Amazon API Gateway -> Core E-Commerce API: Routes client requests securely via mTLS
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads/writes transactional data via TLS over TCP
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Caches exchange rates, promos, and idempotency locks via TLS over TCP
- Core E-Commerce API -> Recommendation Service: Requests personalized recommendations via gRPC
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon SQS: Queues shipping fulfillment tasks via AWS SDK
- Amazon EventBridge -> Core E-Commerce API: Triggers event handlers via Event Bus

## Technology Stack
- Node.js with NestJS: Modular framework for organizing controllers, services, and middleware.
- AWS ECS (Fargate): Scalable serverless container hosting for 1M MAU performance.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Multi-AZ relational database with AWS KMS PII encryption.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): High-performance caching for currency rates and idempotency locks.
- class-validator: Strict DTO validation for OWASP Top-10 security mitigation.

## Rationale
This architecture modularizes core e-commerce domains while enforcing strict security, idempotency, and fault tolerance via circuit breakers. It ensures 99.95% uptime, GDPR/CCPA compliance, and multi-currency support for a global user base.

Recommendation Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Recommendation Service provides personalized book recommendations and promotional merchandising for the Online Bookstore. It processes high-throughput user interactions while meeting strict sub-2-second performance and GDPR/CCPA compliance requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Active Shopper & Marketing Manager**: Primary users and internal personas driving discovery and promotional rules.
- **API Controller**: FastAPI application managing inbound gRPC and REST requests with RBAC.
- **Recommendation Engine**: Python module performing collaborative filtering for "Customers also bought" features.
- **Merchandising & Rules Processor**: Component applying promotional weights for sponsored book placements.
- **Model Store Client**: Fetches pre-computed machine learning models from Amazon S3.
- **Feature Cache Client**: Retrieves real-time user clickstream data from Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).
- **Async Telemetry Publisher**: Background worker managing asynchronous metric collection.

## Relationships
- **Amazon API Gateway -> API Controller**: Routes incoming recommendation requests using mTLS and TLS 1.3.
- **Core E-Commerce API -> API Controller**: Requests personalized recommendations via gRPC.
- **API Controller -> Recommendation Engine & Merchandising Processor**: Coordinates business logic using synchronous in-process method calls.
- **Model Store Client -> Amazon S3**: Fetches models using encrypted AWS SDK calls over HTTPS.
- **Feature Cache Client -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Queries session features via TCP.
- **Async Telemetry Publisher -> Amazon SQS**: Publishes pseudonymized metrics asynchronously via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- **Python with FastAPI**: Powers the core API Controller and asynchronous background workers for high performance.
- **Scikit-learn / LightFM**: Implements collaborative filtering algorithms within the Recommendation Engine.
- **Amazon S3**: Stores pre-computed models secured with AWS KMS encryption.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Delivers low-latency access to real-time user session data.
- **Amazon SQS**: Decouples telemetry publishing to protect critical API latency SLAs.

## Rationale
This component architecture separates high-latency machine learning tasks and telemetry logging from synchronous request paths using asynchronous workers and caching. This design ensures the system scales to 1M MAU while maintaining sub-2-second response times and strict GDPR/CCPA privacy controls.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The architecture implements a globally distributed, high-availability PostgreSQL database system to power the Online Bookstore e-commerce platform. It ensures secure, low-latency data access, strict compliance with data privacy regulations, and robust scalability across multiple AWS regions.

## Key Elements
- Primary Write Instance (Writer Node)
- Read Replica Instances (Multi-AZ / Global)
- Database Encryption & Audit Engine
- Connection Pooler (PgBouncer / Aurora Proxy)
- Global Replication Manager

## Relationships
- Core E-Commerce API -> Connection Pooler: Manages connections [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3 with mTLS]
- Connection Pooler -> Primary Write Instance: Routes transactions [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Connection Pooler -> Read Replica Instances: Routes read queries [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Global Replication Manager -> Global Read Replicas: Synchronizes cross-region data [AWS Dedicated Backbone Network with TLS]
- Database Encryption & Audit Engine -> Amazon CloudWatch / AWS CloudTrail: Streams audit logs [AWS Internal API]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ / Global Database): Chosen for ACID compliance, automated failover, and global read-scaling across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`.
- PgBouncer / Aurora Proxy: Used for efficient connection pooling and preventing thread exhaustion under high traffic.
- AWS KMS: Implemented for encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (CMKs) and automated rotation.
- PostgreSQL `pgaudit` extension: Utilized for high-privilege query tracking and tamper-proof compliance auditing.
- IAM Database Authentication: Replaces native master passwords with short-lived, token-rotated credentials.

## Rationale
This architecture fits requirements by enforcing strict GDPR/CCPA data privacy compliance through encryption, PII masking, and audit logging while guaranteeing 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads globally via read/write splitting and multi-region replication.

Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore system provides scalable e-commerce capabilities for browsing, purchasing physical and electronic books, and viewing recommendations. It utilizes Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) as a high-performance caching and session management layer to meet sub-2-second performance goals under high user load.

## Key Elements
- **Session Store Component**: Manages ephemeral user sessions and shopping carts using Redis Hashes.
- **Product & Catalog Cache Component**: Caches serialized book details and hot categories via the Cache-Aside pattern.
- **Recommendation Cache Component**: Stores pre-computed recommendation lists generated by the Recommendation Service.
- **Core E-Commerce API & Recommendation Service**: Client applications interacting with the cache layer.
- **AWS Infrastructure**: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) Replication Group, AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, and Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

## Relationships
- **Core E-Commerce API -> Session Store Component**: Reads and writes session and cart data [Redis RESP protocol over TLS/TCP]
- **Core E-Commerce API -> Product & Catalog Cache Component**: Retrieves cached catalog data [Redis RESP protocol over TLS/TCP]
- **Recommendation Service -> Recommendation Cache Component**: Populates recommendation lists [Redis RESP protocol over TLS/TCP]

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Multi-AZ replication group with automatic failover for high availability (99.95% uptime).
- **Redis RESP protocol over TLS/TCP**: Secure transport protocol for all inter-container communications.
- **AWS KMS**: Enables mandatory encryption-at-rest for GDPR and CCPA compliance.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Manages and rotates Redis AUTH tokens securely.
- **Amazon CloudWatch Logs**: Captures Redis slow logs and engine logs for security auditing.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads for 1 million MAU by offloading database read traffic and preventing cart loss during failovers. Strict VPC isolation, IAM controls, and AWS KMS encryption fulfill rigorous GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP security constraints.

Amazon EventBridge.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a globally scaled e-commerce platform built on AWS, designed to handle 1M MAU with 99.95% availability while supporting book browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized recommendations. It implements a decoupled, event-driven architecture to ensure low latency and strict GDPR/CCPA compliance across multi-currency transactions.

## Key Elements
* **Book Buyer & Reviewer**: End user browsing catalogues, purchasing books, and leaving reviews.
* **Store Administrator**: Back-office user managing inventory and administrative events.
* **Single-Page Application (SPA)**: React and TypeScript frontend hosted on AWS S3 and CloudFront.
* **Core E-Commerce API**: Node.js (NestJS) application running on AWS ECS (Fargate).
* **Recommendation Service**: Python (FastAPI) application running on AWS ECS (Fargate).
* **Amazon EventBridge**: Event bus containing Default Bus, Custom Event Bus (`bookstore.retail`), Event Rules & Routing, Target Dispatcher, and Event Archive (`bookstore-archive`).
* **Databases & Caching**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ) and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).
* **External Services**: External Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping Provider API.

## Relationships
* **SPA -> Amazon API Gateway**: Routes frontend requests using HTTPS/GraphQL.
* **Amazon API Gateway -> Core E-Commerce API**: Forwards client requests via REST/GraphQL.
* **Core E-Commerce API -> Custom Event Bus**: Publishes domain events (`OrderPlaced`, `ItemReviewed`) via AWS SDK/HTTPS.
* **Custom Event Bus -> Event Archive**: Archives filtered events for compliance via Native EventBridge Rule.
* **Event Rules & Routing -> Amazon SQS**: Buffers routed events for downstream processing via AWS API.
* **Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Manages relational transactional data via PostgreSQL protocol.

## Technology Stack
* **Frontend**: React and TypeScript hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront for rapid global content delivery.
* **Backend Compute**: Node.js (NestJS) and Python (FastAPI) on AWS ECS (Fargate) for scalable containerized microservices.
* **Database & Caching**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ) for ACID-compliant persistence and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for low-latency session and data caching.
* **Event Integration**: Amazon EventBridge with custom buses, rule engines, and encrypted archives for asynchronous, decoupled event-driven workflows.
* **Security & Compliance**: AWS IAM, TLS 1.3, and AWS KMS Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) ensuring data protection, PII payload restriction, and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Rationale
This AWS-native, event-driven architecture decouples heavy background processes like recommendations from synchronous user actions, protecting page load performance under high load (1M MAU). Utilizing managed services like ECS, Aurora, and EventBridge ensures high availability (99.95%), seamless horizontal scalability, and robust security controls tailored to strict regulatory constraints.

Amazon SQS.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore is an Amazon-style e-commerce platform designed for browsing, purchasing physical and electronic books, managing customer reviews, and providing personalized recommendations. The system is architected on AWS to handle high scalability, global multi-region reach, and strict regulatory compliance.]

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer & Reviewer, Store Administrator
- Single-Page Application (React / TypeScript on AWS S3 & CloudFront)
- Amazon API Gateway (REST/GraphQL)
- Core E-Commerce API (Node.js NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Recommendation Service (Python FastAPI on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon EventBridge & Amazon SQS (Standard/FIFO Engine, DLQ, KMS Encryption)
- AWS CloudWatch Alarms & Metrics & AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
- Single-Page Application -> Amazon API Gateway: Forwards user requests [HTTPS / REST & GraphQL]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Core E-Commerce API: Routes business logic requests [HTTP / gRPC]
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads and writes transactional data [TCP / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Caches session data and catalog queries [TCP / Redis Protocol]
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon SQS: Enqueues shipping fulfillment orders [AWS SDK / HTTPS / SigV4]
- Amazon SQS -> Third-Party Shipping Provider API: Dispatches fulfillment requests [HTTPS]
- Standard/FIFO Queue Engine -> CloudWatch Alarms & Metrics: Emits telemetry metrics [AWS Internal]
- CloudWatch Alarms & Metrics -> Logistics Operations Team: Triggers alerts for queue delays and DLQ traffic [HTTPS / PagerDuty Webhooks]

## Technology Stack
- React & TypeScript on AWS S3/CloudFront: Delivers high-performance client-side rendering globally.
- Node.js (NestJS) & Python (FastAPI) on AWS ECS Fargate: Provides containerized, scalable microservices without server management.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ): Ensures robust transactional integrity and high availability.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Delivers ultra-low latency caching for high-performance page loads (<2s).
- Amazon SQS & AWS KMS: Decouples checkout from third-party shipping APIs while securing PII for GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture leverages AWS managed services and containerization on ECS Fargate to effortlessly scale to 1 million monthly active users while maintaining 99.95% uptime. Asynchronous decoupling via Amazon SQS and caching via Redis ensure rapid performance and resilience against third-party API outages.]
